loop: gauntlet: a builder and a separate critic with fresh context per piece. The critic runs ours next to native, names the biggest gap, and the piece loops until the critic picks ours.
bar: native APFS (this Mac) and ext4 (moonscape): cargo build and git status within 1.5x, pjdfstest + fsx + xfstests-generic no worse than native, zero data loss in crash-injection.

items.title: #1 dedup ratio on the real worktree corpus

items.title: #7 chunking, hashing and block store
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Reproduced: F1 put reports Ok for an unreadable block, F2 forged/embedded record poisons an id, F4 a single bit flip in the last SYNCED record makes recovery truncate (delete) it, plus fd-per-pack exhaustion, missing dir fsyncs, O(n) checkpoint under the writer lock, unvalidated alloc, no rust-version, and fsync/BLAKE3 mutants surviving. Builder is fixing with regression tests (durable watermark distinguishes torn tail from corruption). Perf misses stand: chunk+hash ~590 vs 800 MiB/s, verified read ~430 vs 1024 (BLAKE3-bound single thread; 3413 MiB/s at 8 threads).

items.title: #8 Merkle tree and O(1) writable snapshots
items.detail: Builder done: persistent content-addressed B+tree per snapshot in redb, O(1) snapshots (create 20-32 ms fsync-bound, flat within 1.6x at load 73-106), crash harness 3,176 crash points and kill -9 rounds with 0 failures (builder's numbers; I re-ran the default suite: 26 tests pass, builder claimed 39). Design note lists 11 decisions for review, including identity (snapshot id, inode), 2 ms unbatched ops and setattr size shrinking only to a chunk boundary. Critic is attacking crash consistency, panic guard, refcount settlement and the API core needs. docs/v1-meta.md

items.title: #10 garbage collection
#11 Linux FUSE mount
items.detail: Builder done: 22 unit tests (Mac) and 14 mount tests in the Linux VM pass on my re-run, CI green. Defaults: ttl 3600 s, keep_cache, negative ttl 1 s (kernel ignored inval_entry for negative entries per builder), single-threaded request loop. Open: conformance suite through the mount not run, head-of-line blocking risk with a slow core. Critic attacking staleness, POSIX correctness (fsx), lifecycle, forget/inode reuse.

items.title: #12 macOS NFS loopback mount
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Leak: rename over a file never reaps the replaced sidecar inode (200 write-tmp-rename cycles left 202 inodes; 65k-op workload RSS 4 to 899 MB). Biggest gap: AppleDouble sidecars are ~47% of all RPCs and double the inodes (fix: translate sidecars to Vfs xattrs). Latency is RPC count not server speed (server ~99% idle, 8-55 us/RPC; the builder's 3.4/4.1 ms were load noise, minimums 1.0/1.46 ms). Security: any local uid can MNT and use the port (fix: one-shot MNT plus keyed-MAC handles). DoS: 200 half-sent 8 MiB frames took 1.6 GB. Retransmits dropped not replayed; stale handle read another file's bytes after inode reuse; kill -TERM leaves a hung mount. Builder is fixing.

items.title: #13 CLI and Unix-socket control API
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. No cross-user hole, but: no client timeout (status hung 25 s), shutdown waits 6 s for handlers ignoring cancel while the socket stays and new clients hang, unbounded connections (3000 idle -> 3003 threads), slowloris; half-close cancels; unsafe snapshot names accepted (.nfs, ._, case/NFC collisions); no atomic snapshot_reset for treehouse mode (b); import verified is a bare bool. Builder is fixing with regression tests and killing surviving mutants.

#29 cowfs-vfs trait, MemVfs and conformance suite
items.detail: Critic verdict: mergeable as the cowfs contract after fixes, NOT a POSIX suite. Oracle vs real APFS/btrfs/ext4 (100k ops each): directory nlink=2+subdirs only holds on ext4 (btrfs reports 1, APFS 2+entries); setuid, xattr size, non-UTF-8 and NFC assumptions over-specify; oracle bug on rename onto own non-empty ancestor (ENOTEMPTY on Linux); 0.5% of ops have multiple allowed errors and MemVfs errno differs from the real one. 34 new faults: 6 slipped through. No per-check skip. Builder is adding check levels (Posix/Portable/Cowfs), Options::skip with reasons, the 6 checks, faster default tests, MemVfs edge fixes. Public API stays source-compatible for core/fuse/nfs/pathvfs.
